PGE Pricing Plans
We're working to make customer prices more predictable and as low as possible. Here's what we're doing to manage costs and our current pricing plans.

About
Company Info
IMPORTANT NOTICE:
We've filed a request with the Oregon Public Utility Commission to review customer prices. We're actively working to meet the increased energy demand of growing communities to help ensure everyone has safe and reliable power.
Learn more.
Committed to your energy
While PGE does purchase some energy from the wholesale market, most of your power comes from our diverse mix of hydro, thermal, renewables and battery storage. This balanced supply portfolio reduces exposure to sharp market swings, so when we do see volatility, our regulated rates help keep your costs more predictable throughout the year.
⠀
Navigate this page:
Residential power choices
Business power options
Business pricing schedules
What makes up PGE prices?
Base rates
Most notably, base rates cover the cost of maintaining the electric grid.
This includes fixing and replacing old power lines, poles and equipment to help deliver energy to communities safely and reliably.
Power costs
While PGE generates some of the power we serve customers, we also purchase power from across the west and manage our purchased power portfolio to balance customer costs and grid reliability.
Each year, we compare what we expected power to cost with what it actually cost. If costs were lower, customers receive a refund. If they were higher, we may need to recover the difference.
Supplemental charges
Customers may see adjustments on their bills that collect or refund money for new and existing PGE customer programs and safety efforts that support our community, tariffs, state-mandated fees and pass-through costs we’re required to collect. The OPUC regularly reviews these charges when we update our filings.
Residential power choices
Check out our
Power Choices Brochure
for residential customers to see a side-by-side comparison of the prices, fuel sources and environmental impacts of all your options.
Learn more to better
understand your home's electric bill.
Basic Service
This is the plan most customers are on. You’ll continue Basic Service automatically unless you select another option. Pricing is based directly on the costs PGE incurs in providing electric service.
Time of Day Pricing
Save more when you use less electricity between 5-9 p.m. This unique pricing plan offers lower energy prices for using less energy during high demand hours.
Green Future options
Green Future Choice and Green Future Block are re
[DOC 0] https://portlandgeneral.com/about/info/pricing-plans
newable power options that PGE customers can enroll in to support renewable energy in the way that works for you — up to 100%.
Common business pricing schedules
Pricing is based directly on the cost to provide electric service and is regulated by the Oregon Public Utility Commission. The following pricing schedules are the most typical for business customers. Your monthly statement shows your schedule or schedules (some businesses may have more than one).
For medium and large businesses (your bill says Schedule 83, 85 or 89), your Basic Service plan already includes a lower rate for electricity used when demand is typically lower (nights and weekends). Your bill also includes a basic charge, transmission costs, distribution costs and required adjustments.
Schedule 32, small non-residential business customers
This schedule applies to business customers who have not exceeded 30 kW more than twice in the previous 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service). The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use.
Schedule 83, commercial customers
Customers in this schedule have not exceeded 200 kW more than six times in the preceding 13 months and have not exceeded 4,000 kW more than once within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use and the rate at which you use it.
Schedule 85, large commercial customers
Customers in this schedule have exceeded 200 kW more than six times in the preceding 13 months but have not exceeded 4,000 kW more than once within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use and the rate at which you use it.
Schedule 89, industrial customers
Customers in this schedule have a demand that exceeded 4,000 kW at least twice within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount of electricity you use and the rate at which you use it.
Additional business power options
Check out our

for business customers to see a side-by-side comparison of the prices, fuel sources and environmental impacts of all your options.

Time of Use
If you’re a small business that uses most of your electricity on weekends or at night, or you charge an EV overnight, this plan may lower your electricity costs.

Green Future options
Make a difference for the environment and support renewable energy. Go partially or fully renewable with ease, at levels that are right for your business.

Browser Settings
To sign in to your PGE web account, your browser must be set to accept cookies and JavaScript must be enabled.
A cookie is a small text file stored on your computer by a website to give you a unique numeric ID. PGE doesn’t use cookies to track personal information; they are used to enhance your web experience by:
Protecting your privacy and security: We’ll sign you out automatically after 20 idle minutes.
Activating the "Remember Me" feature so your email address is provided automatically the next time you sign in.
PGE also works with third parties that use cookies on our site to conduct visitor surveys and to enable other features.

[DOC 3] https://portlandgeneral.com/2027-general-rate-case
Large energy users pay more
As Oregon's energy needs grow, we're using new regulatory rules to ensure large energy users, such as data centers, pay for the infrastructure they need to grow.
That’s why data centers saw a 29.7% rate increase in 2026; and this new rate case proposes an additional 7.7% increase to continue covering the cost of growth.
These investments benefit all customers by helping to modernize the electric system.
Get involved in a public meeting
You have a voice in the rate review process. The OPUC will facilitate
public meetings
throughout the regulatory process. Customers are encouraged to attend these meetings and provide feedback.

Time of Use
Are you a small business customer and a night owl? You could save with Time of Use.

Home
Pricing Plans
Small business customers
Enrollment in Time of Use is closed to residential customers, but still open for small business customers. If you’re a small business that uses most of your electricity at night or on weekends, or you charge an electric vehicle overnight, this plan may lower your electricity costs.
You pay different rates for electricity you use depending on the time of day, day of week and season. The rate is lower on nights and weekends and higher at high-demand times such as weekday mornings and evenings. If you don’t use electricity primarily on nights and weekends, you may pay more on Time of Use than on the
Basic Service
rate*.
See small business TOU pricing
Residential customers
Residential enrollment in Time of Use closed to new participants on Jan. 1, 2024 and expired for all residential participants after Dec. 31, 2024, at which time remaining participants were placed on the basic service rate.
If you are interested in controlling your energy bill by using less energy during peak times, consider Time of Day pricing. You don’t have to be a night owl to save with Time of Day.
Residential customers
Save with Time of Day
Simply use less energy during the on-peak hours of 5-9 p.m. weekdays to save. All other hours (and all day weekends) are less expensive than Basic Service pricing.
Check it out
*Review the
conditional guarantee
and
eligibility and limits
.

Pricing Plans
Market-Based Pricing
Upcoming election window
November annual election window
The next opportunity to return to PGE’s standard service pricing is from
Nov. 16 at 2p.m. through Nov. 23, 2026 at 5p.m.
Changes would be effective Jan. 1, 2027. This window is the only time you can return to, or leave, PGE standard service pricing for service in 2026 if you are currently served by an Electricity Service Supplier or on PGE’s Daily Market Pricing.
For more information on the November election window, see our
FAQs.
You can modify your plan by reaching out to
business.outreach@pgn.com
or by
logging in to your business account
— if you do not have an account and need assistance registering, please contact your account manager or the PGE Business Services team at 800-822-1077.
What is it
How do I sign up
When do I sign up
Depending on your organization’s management strategy, you may want to consider your options regarding your pricing plan. You can choose how long you want to be on a market-based plan and who you buy electricity from. These choices can have a significant and long-term impact on your company’s future energy costs, so it’s important to have the information you need to make the best decision for your business.
Visit our
fact sheet
to review details and FAQs on selecting your electricity supplier.
Your options
Stay on PGE’s standard service
. It’s open to all businesses within our service area and you don’t need to take any action or sign contracts to stay on it.
Choose short-term market-based power.
Choose long-term market-based power.
PGE’s Daily Market Pricing
If you choose PGE’s Daily Market pricing, your prices are based on the Intercontinental Exchange Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) Daily on- and off- peak Electricity Firm Price Index (ICE-Mid-C Firm Index). Prices will vary, as they re
[DOC 5] https://portlandgeneral.com/about/info/pricing-plans/market-based-pricing
flect the supply and demand in the energy market. Daily pricing information is available for a fee at
theice.com
and in other financial publications.
Direct Access through an ESS
With this option, you will be electing to purchase power from a third-party Electricity Service Supplier (ESS).*
These ESSs are registered to work with PGE:
Avangrid Renewables, LLC
Calpine Energy Solutions, LLC
Constellation NewEnergy
Shell Energy North America
Brookfield Renewable Energy Marketing US, LLC
They may contact you to offer their services. Delivery charges, adjustments, taxes and other standard fees regulated by the Oregon Public Utility Commission will still apply and reflect on your PGE bill.
*PGE cannot guarantee the accuracy of ESS claims and their ability to serve load now or in the future. If you have questions or would like to validate claims regarding PGE's standard service pricing, please contact
business.outreach@pgn.com
.
We’re here to help
Email your PGE representative at
business.outreach@pgn.com
or call PGE Business Services at
800-822-1077
if you have questions about any of your pricing choices.
We’ve got your back
No matter who you choose to buy electricity from, it will still be delivered over PGE’s system of power lines, poles and substations. We’ll still be here for you, delivering electricity safely and reliably, just like we always have.
Transition adjustments
If you opt for Daily Market Pricing or Direct Access, a
transition adjustment
will be added to your bill. Transition adjustments are different for each election window, and can be a charge or credit, depending on the market.

Browser Settings
To sign in to your PGE web account, your browser must be set to accept cookies and JavaScript must be enabled.
A cookie is a small text file stored on your computer by a website to give you a unique numeric ID. PGE doesn’t use cookies to track personal information; they are used to enhance your web experience by:
Protecting your privacy and security: We’ll sign you out automatically after 20 idle minutes.
Activating the "Remember Me" feature so your email address is provided automatically the next time you sign in.
PGE also works with third parties that use cookies on our site to conduct visitor surveys and to enable other features.

Pricing Plans
Understanding Our Pricing
How prices are determined
Like all investor-owned utilities in Oregon, PGE undergoes a price-setting process with the Oregon Public Utility Commission, called a rate case, when it needs to ask the Commission to set or change the overall prices customers pay for electric service. PGE bases its proposed prices on forecasts of what it believes its future costs to provide service will be, plus a reasonable rate of return.
PGE customers have a voice in the rate case process. With support from PGE, the
OPUC
holds open houses for the community on every rate case considered. Customers are encouraged to attend these open houses and provide feedback. The OPUC then sets prices for residential and business customers at levels it determines to be just and reasonable.
Annually, in between rate cases, the OPUC also adjusts prices to reflect the projected net cost of the power needed to serve customers for the year ahead and make any other necessary changes. This includes the cost for PGE to generate its own energy — which is affected by prices for raw fuel like coal and natural gas — and how weather will affect the output of hydroelectric and wind generators. Price adjustments also include the predicted cost to buy supplemental energy from other suppliers on the wholesale power market.
The Public Utility Commission of Oregon approved several Advice Filings which will be effective on January 1, 2025. In addition, PGE filed the UE 435 General Rate Revision Compliance Filing effective January 1, 2025. The approved changes to Supplemental Schedule and the results of UE 435 General Rate Revision effective January 1, 2025, result in an overall revenue increase of $188 million. Total rate increase for January 1, 2025, for residential customers is a 5.6% increase on average, commercial customers will experience a 7.6% on average increase, and industrial customers will experience a 6.0%
[DOC 6] https://portlandgeneral.com/about/info/pricing-plans/understanding-our-pricing
 on average increase.
Common business pricing schedules
Pricing is based directly on the cost to provide electric service and is regulated by the Oregon Public Utility Commission. The following pricing schedules are the most typical for business customers. Your monthly statement shows your schedule or schedules (some businesses may have more than one).
For medium and large businesses (your bill says Schedule 83, 85 or 89), your Basic Service plan already includes a lower rate for electricity used when demand is typically lower (nights and weekends). Your bill also includes a basic charge, transmission costs, distribution costs and required adjustments.
Schedule 32, small non-residential business customers
This schedule applies to business customers who have not exceeded 30 kW more than twice in the previous 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service). The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use.
Schedule 83, commercial customers
Customers in this schedule have not exceeded 200 kW more than six times in the preceding 13 months and have not exceeded 4,000 kW more than once within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use and the rate at which you use it.
Schedule 85, large commercial customers
Customers in this schedule have exceeded 200 kW more than six times in the preceding 13 months but have not exceeded 4,000 kW more than once within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount you use and the rate at which you use it.
Schedule 89, industrial customers
Customers in this schedule have a demand that exceeded 4,000 kW at least twice within the prior 13 months (or once with seven months or less of service).
The price you pay for electricity is determined by the amount of electricity you use and the rate at which you use it.

Google Analytics sets this cookie to calculate visitor, session and campaign data and track site usage for the site's analytics report. The cookie stores information anonymously and assigns a randomly generated number to recognise unique visitors.
Cookie
_gid
Duration
1 day
Description
Google Analytics sets this cookie to store information on how visitors use a website while also creating an analytics report of the website's performance. Some of the collected data includes the number of visitors, their source, and the pages they visit anonymously.
Cookie

1 minute
Description

Browser Settings
To sign in to your PGE web account, your browser must be set to accept cookies and JavaScript must be enabled.
A cookie is a small text file stored on your computer by a website to give you a unique numeric ID. PGE doesn’t use cookies to track personal information; they are used to enhance your web experience by:
Protecting your privacy and security: We’ll sign you out automatically after 20 idle minutes.
Activating the "Remember Me" feature so your email address is provided automatically the next time you sign in.
PGE also works with third parties that use cookies on our site to conduct visitor surveys and to enable other features.
